questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when following a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You must go slowly through the intersection.
You must stop, then go when the way is clear.
You must stop, then go when the light changes to green or a green arrow appears.
You may turn in the direction the arrow is pointing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop, then go when the light changes to green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must come to a full stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: How should you prepare for what is ahead on the road?

options.text: Look at the entire road and all sides of the road.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Keep your left foot resting lightly on the brake.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all sides of the road.
questions.explanation: To handle dangerous situations, you must spot problems before you reach them. Look far ahead, but also scan the entire road and the sides of the road. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: When can you legally pass another vehicle on the right?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you must drive off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right of a vehicle turning left or waiting to turn left if there is a passing lane available. You can also pass on the right on a multilane road with two or more lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without hard braking. Then very carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for nearby traffic when re-entering the road.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up as fast as you can.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go through the intersection. However, first let any pedestrians and traffic still in the intersection cross.

questions.question: You are angry after an incident at work. What should you do before driving?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you do not think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to release your anger.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Stop for drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to calm down before driving. Driving while angry is dangerous to yourself and others on the road.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to see if your blind spot is clear. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Using snow tires helps your vehicle on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season and requires extra care. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This chevron sign warns that the road curves sharply in the direction the arrow points. In this case, it curves left. You may see several of these signs along the curve.

questions.question: It is best to keep a space cushion:

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your vehicle on all sides. This gives you time to react to dangers. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment depends on:

options.text: Whether you drink beer instead of wine.
Whether you drink wine instead of beer.
Whether you drink hard ciders and mixed drinks.
How much alcohol is in your bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much alcohol is in your bloodstream.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol hurts your reflexes and judgment. The type of alcohol does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, and ambulances using sirens or air horns with red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so make sure the way is clear before you move.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, you should:

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Not let other cars pass you.
Use your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. On a two-lane road, if traffic backs up behind you, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive slowly when road conditions require it.

questions.question: If you are driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle share half a lane.
Pass the motorcycle in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give motorcycles a full lane width. Even if there seems to be room to share a lane, the motorcycle needs space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when the roads are wet.
Keep your tires at the right air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your car slides on water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases this risk.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that their mirrors cannot see.

questions.question: A traffic light showing a green arrow with a red light means:

options.text: You may only drive straight.
You may only drive in the direction the arrow points.
You must wait for a solid green light to go any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only drive in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction of the arrow, if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen when one driver does not see another vehicle or makes an unexpected move. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at a four-way stop sign at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if you and another driver arrive at the same time, yield to the driver on your right. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: Your tires work less well as you drive faster.
Good tires are not affected by water.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slower speeds make the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires work less well as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: When you drive fast on a wet road, your tires cannot remove water effectively. At very high speeds, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane—slide on a film of water.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At an open intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which must you obey before the other three?

options.text: A steady red light.
A police officer.
A stop sign.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer.
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions override all signs, signals, and road markings. Other traffic control people include fire police, highway work zone flag persons, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or in a curve because few vehicles are coming.
By driving on the road shoulder.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves—you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never drive on the shoulder to pass. You cannot cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow.
White.
Red.
Black.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let them know you're passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up to pull in front of them quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them plenty of room. Bicyclists have less protection than drivers. Passing too fast can push them off course.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive no faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use headlights when visibility is 500 feet or less. Always use low beam headlights in fog or rain. High beams reflect light back at you and make visibility worse.

questions.question: How should you reduce the glare from oncoming headlights at night?

options.text: Look straight ahead.
Look over your shoulder.
Look at the center of the road.
Look to the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming drivers don't dim their lights, look at the right side of the road ahead. Don't look directly at the headlights—the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Honk at incoming traffic.
Always stay at your current speed.
Speed up to avoid congestion.
Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.
questions.explanation: When traffic is merging into your road, move to another lane if it's safe. This helps entering vehicles join safely.
